title: Alert State
description: The monitor's memory. Because each monitor cycle runs as a fresh session with no conversational history, ALL continuity lives here. A monitor that does not read and write this file will re-alert the same trigger every cycle — this file is the difference between a useful desk and one the client mutes before 10am.

watchlist_ref.description: Path to the watchlist this state is tracking. If it does not match, the monitor must halt rather than guess.

cycles.description: One entry per monitor run. Append-only. Gives you a latency and coverage record for free, and makes a missed cycle visible instead of silent.

errors.description: Endpoints that failed this cycle. Recorded, not swallowed. A trigger that could not be evaluated is NOT the same as a trigger that did not fire, and the two must never be conflated.

not_evaluated.description: Trigger ids the monitor could not evaluate this cycle, with the reason. These are reported to the client as gaps.

fired.description: Keyed by trigger id. The dedup ledger.

position_state.description: Keyed by position id. Tracks what the client has already been told about each open position so the desk does not repeat itself.

stage_notified.description: Each stage is announced once. Re-announcing 'approaching stop' every 15 minutes is noise, not risk management.

suppressed.description: Set when max_fires is reached. The trigger stays evaluated (so the record is complete) but stops alerting.

observed_values.description: What the field actually read each time it fired. This is what lets you grade trigger quality at the close instead of guessing.
